title: Use @grafana/ui copyTextToClipboard instead of a bespoke clipboard implementation
answers: How do I copy text to the clipboard in Grafana UI code?
Why are there multiple clipboard copy functions / which one should I use?
body:
Symptom: three near-identical clipboard-copy implementations existed (ClipboardButton's copyText, explore.ts's copyStringToClipboard, notebook export's copyToClipboard), each with slightly different Safari/secure-context handling.
Root cause: no shared util, so clipboard logic was copy-pasted and could drift.
Fix pattern: all clipboard writes now go through the single exported `copyTextToClipboard` in packages/grafana-ui/src/utils/copyToClipboard.ts (re-exported from packages/grafana-ui/src/index.ts). New code that needs to copy text should import it from `@grafana/ui` rather than writing a new textarea/execCommand fallback or calling navigator.clipboard directly.
Constraints: it accepts `string | Promise<string>` and an optional element ref for the fallback's append target; it returns a promise that rejects on failure, so callers must handle that (see related note on awaiting it).
applies: Any Grafana frontend code (core app or grafana-ui) that needs to copy text to the system clipboard

Accepts `string | Promise<string>` and optional element ref for the fallback target; returns a promise that rejects on failure, requiring callers to handle errors. Replaces bespoke clipboard logic (ClipboardButton.copyText, explore.ts.copyStringToClipboard, notebook export.copyToClipboard) that had drifted in Safari/secure-context handling. Applies to any Grafana frontend code (core app or grafana-ui) that needs to copy text to the system clipboard.
